Commentary.Commentary: Now then, the target is a challenging one and Nigeria will have to bat really well if they are to chase this down. Canada are probably favorites to defend it and anything other than that will be a surprise. Do join us in a short while for the second innings.

Nitish Kumar is down for a quick interview. Thinks his approach was what got him going after a not so good start. Feels that they have gotten to the target they wanted to achieve and he is confident that they can defend this. Further adds that he does not feel dew is a big factor tonight and they should look to stick to their basics. Ends by saying that they want to be known as a positive and aggressive team and he thinks that they are going in the right direction.

The Nigerian bowling wasn't that great. Except for Abiodun Abioye and Daniel Ajekun, the rest were very inconsistent with their lines and lengths. Their fielding also did not help as there were too many misfields and dropped catches. Overall, they need to improve a lot in this aspect of the game.

Some lusty blows in the last few overs have seen Canada post a total which one feels is just above par. However, they could have scored a little more after their top order got them off to a decent start. However, they did lose their way in the middle, an excellent cameo by Tariq and a stable knock from Kumar have given them the score which they would have wanted after electing to bowl.

We are all set to begin. The Nigerian players are out in the middle. Rodrigo Thomas and Navneet Dhaliwal will open the batting for Canada. Isaac Okpe will start the proceedings for Nigeria.

Toss - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Canada. Canada have won the toss and have elected to bat.

Hello and welcome everyone for Match 18 of the  ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier in Abu Dhabi between Canada and Nigeria. Both teams have played one game each at the moment and the results were contrasting for them. On one hand, Canada registered a thumping win while on the other hand, Nigeria were thrashed. The Canadian team looks quite strong on paper and will be the favourites here while the Nigerian boys would have to play out of their skins to compete. Let's hope for a good battle between bat and ball.
